title: Angloform word definition (ADR 0061)
description: One file per lemma, seed/definitions/<lemma>.yaml. Shape-only — parse_definition (crates/grammar) separately checks that "definition", every "rejected[].advice", and every "antonym"/"rejected[].redirects" reference resolve to real Angloform/real words. lexgen runs both checks (ADR 0061).

category.description: The Category of the Lemma (ADR 0001) — which grammar entry point checks "definition".

forms.description: Irregular Surface Forms only (ADR 0001) — a word whose regular-rule form is wrong or identical to its own lemma (e.g. "sheep"). Never list a regular form.

definition.description: A genus/differentia fragment (NOUN), a bare verb phrase (VERB_TRANS/VERB_INTRANS), or a bare adjective phrase (ADJ) — never a full sentence. Checked by parse_definition against "category".

antonym.description: One lemma with (roughly) the opposite meaning. Curated by a person, not derived. Must resolve to an existing word; not required to be reciprocal.

rejected.description: Every attested-but-disabled sense of this lemma, replacing the old free-text seed.json "reject"/"reject_advice".

tag.description: The Form Tag this Surface Form gets (the same tag strings lexicon.tsv already uses, e.g. "NOUN_PL", "VERB_TRANS_ED").

form.description: The literal spelling — the Surface Form itself.

category.description: The disabled sense's own Category (e.g. this lemma is enabled as NOUN but attested and rejected as VERB).

redirects.description: 1+ substitute words. Each one's meaning is looked up from ITS OWN definition file — never restated here.

advice.description: Only when no substitute word exists (redirects absent). A parse_definition-checked Angloform micro-definition of the disabled sense, using the same shape "category" implies.

gap.description: A real, nameable absence: no already-enabled word covers this attested sense (checked with scripts/word-check.py, not asserted). Renders as a fixed, templated message, never hand-authored prose — the structural alternative to "advice" for words still mid-bootstrap (docs/lexicon-authoring-format-2026-09-07.md's "Gap" concept). Not a permanent verdict: re-check with word-check.py as the enabled vocabulary grows.
